title: U.S. CISA Adds Four Critical Flaws to Known Exploited Vulnerabilities List
content: CISA added four critical flaws impacting Apache, Cisco, SAP, and VMware to its KEV, with evidence of active exploitation. These vulnerabilities could lead to remote code execution and unauthorized access.

title: Signal Restricts AI Access to Prevent Chat Reading
content: Signal blocks AI agents from reading private chats via screenshots on Android and iOS, though protection is incomplete. This affects users of iOS 27 and Android versions with Signal installed, aiming to mitigate unauthorized access but faces technical limitations.

title: 6 Critical F5 BIG-IP Vulnerabilities Could Let Hackers Disrupt Websites and Execute Malicious Code
content: F5 released emergency fixes for six critical BIG-IP vulnerabilities allowing remote attackers to disrupt websites and execute malicious code. The flaws affect traffic-handling configurations, potentially crashing the Traffic Management Microkernel. Affected versions include BIG-IP, BIG-IP Next for Kubernetes, and BIG-IP Cloud-Native Network Functions. Organizations should apply specific hotfixes based on their product and configuration to mitigate these risks.

title: WhatsApp Android Flaws Could Let Hackers Delete Users’ Files and Expose IP Addresses
content: Three WhatsApp Android vulnerabilities could allow attackers to delete local files, expose IP addresses, or bypass security checks. Of three flaws, only IP exposure was flagged for potential abuse. Users should update to the latest version to mitigate risks.

title: PHP releases critical patches for 18 security flaws following PHP2Shell
content: PHP addressed 18 security issues, including a critical request smuggling flaw, across its core engine, session handling, and CGI protocol. Enterprises must patch all supported versions quickly to prevent RCE and other severe exploits.

title: CTO of RansomwareHelp Indicted for Wire Fraud
content: The CTO and co-founder of ransomwarehelp.com, a company falsely claiming to restore data locked by ransomware, was indicted for wire fraud after being caught paying ransomware groups for decryption keys and charging victims markups. The company targeted small to medium-sized businesses, using fraudulent claims to extort significant sums. The case highlights ongoing efforts by authorities to crack down on fraudulent security firms in the ransomware space.

title: F5 releases critical out-of-band patches for BIG-IP products
content: F5 has released critical out-of-band patches for BIG-IP APM and iRules, five of which are rated 9.8 in severity. These patches address stack-based buffer overflows that could lead to remote code execution. BIG-IP APM and iRules handle application traffic and security, respectively. Administrators should install the patches to mitigate risks.

PHP 8.6 was released to patch seven critical remote code execution (RCE) flaws and strengthen security settings. It affects all PHP-based applications, including WordPress, Laravel, and Symfony. New features like Strict Mode, HttpOnly flag, and SameSite settings make exploitation more difficult. Administrators must ensure configurations aren't overridden by other files to fully benefit.
title: PHP 8.6 Introduces Security Enhancements to Mitigate Exploits

content: Multiple vulnerabilities in Mitel MiCollab could allow for arbitrary code execution. This unified communications and collaboration platform for enterprises could be significantly impacted, potentially leading to data modification or deletion and unauthorized account creation. Mitigation includes timely patching and reducing administrative privileges.
title: Multiple Vulnerabilities in Mitel MiCollab Could Allow for Arbitrary Code Execution

content: A vulnerability in VMware vCenter could enable unauthenticated attackers to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access. VMware vCenter Server is a centralized management platform for VMware vSphere environments. Successful exploitation could allow attackers to install programs, view, change, or delete data, or create new accounts with full user rights.
title: Vulnerability in VMware vCenter Could Permit Authentication Bypass
Visa, Mastercard data breach includes mobile numbers, BIN prefixes, and booking details but no card numbers
content: Visa and Mastercard suffered a data breach by the ransomware and extortion group n0n, leaking customer data including mobile numbers, BIN prefixes, and booking details. No card numbers, passwords, or home addresses were found. This data could be used in social engineering attacks. The breach involved a third-party provider, potentially Qubole, as the timing matches a disclosed Qubole supply-chain campaign. Financial institutions are investigating.

title: Researcher plants 2 million canaries in AI supply chain to test data leakage
content: A researcher embedded 2 million digital tripwires in AI services to test data leakage, uncovering widespread privacy violations. Sensitive information, including AWS keys and SSH passwords, leaked through AI routers. This experiment highlights the risks in AI supply chains and the need for better security measures.

Signal has barred AI agents like Google Gemini and Apple Siri from accessing messages without explicit user permission. This follows privacy concerns and measures like blocking screenshots to prevent AI systems from gaining access to private communications. Users can disable these protections, risking exposure of their data. Apple and Google are implementing more granular controls on macOS and iOS to limit AI access, but the issue of AI agents undermining privacy remains significant.
title: Signal restricts AI agents to protect user privacy

content: The podcast discusses an AI fraud kingpin, AI detection tools used by the Department of Justice against defense lawyers, and an AI agent suing Meta. No clear technical incident occurred but covers emerging AI legal and security issues.
title: Podcast: Insights into AI Fraud and Legal Implications
Vulnerabilities in nginx Affecting Cisco Products: November 2026
content: nginx announced fixes for multiple critical vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-113425, CVE-2026-121810, CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-123634) in releases 1.9.5 through 1.31.8, affecting nginx and Cisco products. Critical remote code execution is possible. Cisco released Security Advisories.

title: Cisco Security Advisory - Update 1 for Vulnerabilities
content: Cisco released updates for multiple products including Cisco IOS XR Software, Cisco Expressway Series, Snort 3, Cisco Cyber Vision, Cisco Secure FTD Software, Cisco Secure Client, and Cisco Emergency Responder due to vulnerabilities. CISA added CVE-2026-76466 to their KEV database. Users are advised to apply necessary updates.

SAP released security advisories addressing multiple vulnerabilities in various products, with CVE-2025-42884 added to CISA’s KEV database. Impacted products include SAP NetWeaver, HANA, and Business One. Users should review advisories, apply updates, and mitigate risks.
title: SAP Security Advisory – November 2025 Monthly Rollup (AV25-738) – Update 1
WhatsApp Addresses Security Flaws, Including Android Bug Suspected in Scams
content: WhatsApp patched 3 security flaws, with one Android bug suspected in scam messages. The vulnerability (CVE-2026-23871) involved incomplete validation of external ad-reply URLs. Affected: WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business Android users. Mitigation: Update to the latest version (2.26.17.4 or later).

title: Multiple Vulnerabilities in PHP Could Allow for Remote Code Execution
content: Multiple vulnerabilities in PHP could allow for remote code execution. PHP is a widely used web development language. Exploitation could result in unauthenticated remote code execution in the context of the affected service account, potentially leading to data loss or system compromise.

Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) is a heap out-of-bounds write in the AVX-512 Base64 decoder. Affected Java versions include 17.0.6 and later, 18 to 27, and Oracle’s 8u511 Enterprise Performance Pack. No exploitation in the wild as of November 17, 2026. Mitigate by applying -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics or using TruRisk Eliminate from Qualys, which targets affected hosts and applies the mitigation automatically. Patching remains the recommended solution.
title: Mitigate Java4Shell with TruRisk Eliminate

content: Java4Shell, a heap out-of-bounds write in HotSpot’s AVX-512 Base64 decoder, allows pre-auth RCE in Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, etc. Oracle released patches on Nov 17, 2026. Untested mitigation options include starting JVM with -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics and TruRisk Eliminate, which targets affected hosts. No wild exploitation reported yet.
title: Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) Exploit Mitigation
Chinese-nexus actor’s Cairn AI agents found a zero-day on their own
content: A Chinese-nexus threat actor used autonomous AI agents to target universities, finding and exploiting a zero-day vulnerability in an open-source medical imaging application. The agents gained full control of a server within 11 minutes, demonstrating the speed and capability of agentic offensive operations. Defenders should prioritize high-confidence detections and automated responses.

Suspected Chinese spies deployed AI agents to autonomously find and exploit a zero-day in MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging AI application, gaining full control of a university server. The agents also attempted multiple unsuccessful attacks using other vulnerabilities. Amazon notified the project maintainers, who released a fix. This case highlights the use of AI in advanced persistent threats (APTs).
title: China attackers used AI agents to exploit a zero-day in MONAI Label, gaining full control of a university server
UK operation mitigates cyber-attack risk on European supermarkets' fridges and freezers
content: A UK government cybersecurity operation prevented an attack on fridges and freezers in supermarkets, warehouses, restaurants, petrol stations, and stadiums. The attack would have mirrored recent European breaches causing significant damage. Researchers warn many retailers remain vulnerable.

Microsoft was recognized as a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for SIEM. The company’s Sentinel SIEM brings together security data, advanced analytics, and threat intelligence to help organizations protect their digital estates. The Integrated Security Operations Center (ISOC) integrates SIEM with XDR, threat intelligence, and AI agents for faster threat detection and response.
title: Microsoft Named a Leader in 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for SIEM
Bazuka Android Malware Uses Fake Screen Overlays for Credential Theft and Device Control
content: Bazuka, a newly discovered Android malware framework, uses fake screen overlays to steal credentials and control devices. ThreatFabric identified it during an investigation into an NFC-relay banking Trojan. Victims are targeted for large-scale victim management and control.

Microsoft was recognized as a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for SIEM. Microsoft Sentinel, a cloud-native SIEM, combines security data, advanced analytics, and threat intelligence to enhance visibility and response. The Integrated Security Operations Center (ISOC) integrates SIEM capabilities with XDR and threat intelligence for faster threat detection and response.
title: Microsoft Named a Leader in Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for SIEM

content: More than 100 Debian packages retained distrusted CA certificates after updates, affecting applications that rely on their own trust stores. Debian developers are discussing potential solutions. Administrators must ensure their systems use the latest ca-certificates update and check trust settings in various applications.
title: Over 100 Debian Packages Still Contain Distrusted CA Certificates Despite Security Updates

content: Microsoft is investigating issues with attachment uploads in New Outlook, while uploads in Outlook on the web and classic Outlook are unaffected. Users can switch to these alternatives or wait for the fix. The impact is limited, and no regions or user counts are specified. The issue is being tracked in the Microsoft 365 admin center under EX1561765.
title: Microsoft Investigates Attachment Upload Failures in New Outlook
Dutch Data Protection Authority Warns of Safety Risks in AI Smart Glasses
content: The Dutch Data Protection Authority (AP) warns against buying AI-powered smart glasses due to safety issues, including incorrect advice and privacy risks. Tests revealed misinterpretations of safety warnings, potential data processing outside EU, and the ability for nearby individuals to connect to and view recordings without permission. AP advises politicians to consider policy development for high-risk AI products.

title: Behind the Blog: Keeping It Together
content: This week's Behind the Blog discusses online discourse toxicity, focusing on the public's sudden interest in a hippo situation at a zoo, leading to a surge in amateur expertise and heated debate. No technical impact reported, but highlights the impact of online discourse on public interest and community dynamics.

Moxa announces vulnerabilities in several product series, including ioLogik E1200, EDS-E, IKS, ICS, PT, SDS, TWS, and TN. Affected firmware versions are all prior to v4.0. Users are advised to update to the latest firmware to mitigate potential exploits.
title: Moxa issues security advisory for multiple product series
Still tracking company passwords in spreadsheets? You’re flying blind.
content: Centralized password management improves credential visibility, identifies security risks, and simplifies secure password sharing. IT administrators using spreadsheets are at risk of weak, reused, or compromised credentials.
Noteworthy stories include EU cyber sanctions, malware targeting CACs, and Gemini agents targeted by Epoch AI. Impact on energy firms and supercomputers, with ongoing malware exploitation.
title: In Other News: Norwegian Energy Firm Cyberattacks, Supercomputer Hack, New Nightmare Eclipse Exploit

content: Noteworthy stories that might have slipped under the radar: EU sanctions NoName057, malware targets CACs, Gemini agents targeted Epoch AI.
title: In Other News: Norwegian Energy Firm Cyberattacks, Supercomputer Hack, New Nightmare Eclipse Exploit
Critical Apache Tomcat Flaw Allows Remote Attackers to Join Server Clusters Without Authentication
content: A critical flaw in Apache Tomcat, tracked as CVE-2026-133325, allows remote attackers to join trusted server clusters without authentication. Affects versions 11.0.28-29, 10.1.62, and 9.0.124. Requires TLS 1.3 with a pre-shared key. Mitigation: Switch to TLS 1.2 with the pre-shared key enabled.

Signal is updating its iOS and Android apps to block screenshots to prevent AI assistants like Siri and Gemini from accessing private conversations. This update aims to protect user privacy by preventing AI systems from reading chats.
title: Signal restricts screenshots to prevent AI assistants from accessing private chats

content: The US launches the Threat Disruption Center to coordinate efforts between investigators and companies to disrupt scam networks targeting Americans. It aims to warn victims sooner, pause payments, and freeze funds. Victims should report scams promptly to the FBI’s IC3 to maximize the chance of recovering lost funds.
title: US Launches Threat Disruption Center to Combat Scams

content: The US launches the Threat Disruption Center to connect investigators with companies to help prevent scams, freeze funds, and take down malicious infrastructure. It aims to warn victims sooner and intervene before stolen money disappears. Beneficiaries include anyone targeted by scams, cybercrime, and sextortion.
title: US Launches Threat Disruption Center to Combat Scams

content: Hackers deployed a malware campaign called CyberLeek using over 355 domains to distribute fake GTA 6 PC launchers, which deliver malicious software. The campaign targets gamers looking for early releases. Visitors may download a ZIP archive containing a disguised installer. Mitigation includes deleting unopened files and checking for unusual activity if the installer was run.
title: Hackers Use 355 Domains to Spread Fake GTA 6 PC Launchers Delivering Malware

content: A ransomware group leaked personal information, including emails and phone numbers, from third-party service providers linked to Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan Chase customers. No payment data was reported exposed, but the data could be used by scammers. JPMorgan, Visa, and Mastercard disclosed incidents involving third-party providers. Customers are advised to verify messages and use official channels to protect accounts.
title: Hackers leak data linked to Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan customers

content: A ransomware group leaked data including emails, phone numbers, and travel/dining bookings from third-party service providers of Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan. No payment data was exposed. Companies acknowledged incidents but reported no impact on their payment networks. Customers are advised to verify messages independently and consider credit freezes for identity protection.
title: Hackers leak data linked to Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan customers

content: Hackers rebuilt the SoftEther VPN Bridge, renaming it NtMonitor, to facilitate stealthy access to government networks. Webworm, a China-aligned espionage group, used this tool to maintain post-breach access without triggering standard security measures. Researchers from Rapid7 identified the modified tool and provided guidance on detection and mitigation.
title: Hackers Turn Legitimate VPN Software Into a Stealthy Tool for Spying on Government Networks

content: A heap buffer overflow in OpenSSL’s Base64 encoding function can corrupt application memory when processing large inputs. The vulnerability (CVE-2026-121481) affects OpenSSL versions 4.0.0 to 4.0.3 and 4.1.0. Security teams should check for large untrusted data use and enforce input limits. Update to OpenSSL 4.0.4 or 4.1.1 to mitigate risk.
title: OpenSSL Hit by Critical 9.8 Heap Buffer Overflow Vulnerability in Base64 Encoding Function

content: A vulnerability in KVM allowed researchers to access 127 GB of a cloud server's memory from a guest VM. Affects AMD hosts with nested virtualization enabled. Mitigation involves updating to fixed kernels.
title: Linux KVM Flaw CVE-2026-99312 Lets Guest VMs Access Host Memory on AMD Hosts
AI Autonomy Gains Traction in Security Operations Centers
content: Security leaders plan to increase AI autonomy in SOC, with 60% expecting full comfort in autonomously acting on low-risk security actions within 12 months. This initiative is the top ranking for 2027. The technical impact includes enhanced automation and potentially reduced human oversight.

The UK government served Apple with a secret Technical Capability Notice (TCN) demanding access to end-to-end encrypted iCloud data, contradicting the NCND policy. Apple revoked Advanced Data Protection (ADP) for UK users, while US officials urged opposition. The court has not disclosed the TCN's precise content, citing national security concerns. A substantive hearing is scheduled for 2027.
title: UK Court Confirms Demand for Apple iCloud Backdoor
BYOD Ransomware Hackers Play Audio Ransom Messages on Computers Across Hospitals and Universities
content: Ransomware hackers played audio ransom messages on computers in hospitals and universities, affecting the University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center and Vanderbilt University. The incidents disrupted operations, with ambulances diverted and clinics canceling appointments. BYOD claimed to compromise 36,000 systems, though this remains unverified. Universities warned of unexpected login prompts and advised password resets. The technical impact included unexpected audio playback and repeated login requests. Mitigation focused on endpoint security and user education.

title: Hackers Use AI-Powered ARTEX Framework to Automate Cyberattacks Without Relying on Zero-Day Exploits
content: Attackers are using an AI-driven tool called ARTEX to automate cyberattacks by hunting for ordinary security mistakes and continuously acting on them. This has led to rapid unauthorized access in under three hours. The framework is open-source and connects a large language model to hacking tools, enabling automated decision-making and actions. Defenders should limit access to exposed tools and APIs, set strict API controls, and test unusual API usage. Indicators of compromise include backdoored Docker images and specific user agents.

title: Windows 11 passkey bug causes authentication failure
content: A Windows 11 passkey bug leads to authentication failure messages on Android devices even after successful sign-ins. A fix is available for versions 25H2 and 26H2. Affects Microsoft Authenticator and Google Password Manager, but not iPhone users. Until patched, users should ignore Android error messages if sign-in is successful on the PC.

title: SonicWall Warns of Security Risks for Unsupported Gen 6 Firewalls
content: SonicWall advises replacing Generation 6 firewalls due to security risks from AI-assisted attacks. Retiring these devices is crucial to avoid exploitation of critical flaws. Customers are urged to replace and secure their devices promptly.

title: Hackers Exploit Critical Cisco Expressway Flaw, Breach Four Devices and Reach Internal Network
content: Threat actors exploited CVE-2026-76466, a critical vulnerability in Cisco Expressway, breaching four devices and accessing an internal network. CVSS score 9.8. A PoC was released shortly before the breach.

title: BADBOX 3.0 malware used Android TV boxes for ad fraud
content: BADBOX 3.0 malware compromised Android TV boxes to generate 40 billion daily bid requests for ad fraud. Advertisers paid for placements on home internet connections. Mitigation involved disrupting the operation.

title: No Straight Lines: The value of a different career journey
content: Article emphasizes the value of diverse career paths in technology, promoting resilience, curiosity, and inclusivity through community support. No technical incident or cybersecurity threat mentioned.
The Digital Café assists the Nauheim community in building tech confidence. Sophos volunteers contribute 40 hours each to support digital inclusion. No technical impact or mitigation described.
title: The Digital Café
Palo Alto Confirms Critical Java Vulnerability Affects Privilege Threat Analytics and Remote Access Connector
content: A critical Java vulnerability (CVE-2026-114938) affects Palo Alto Networks' Privilege Threat Analytics, Remote Access Connector, and on-premises HTML5 Gateway. Successful exploitation could lead to remote code execution. Customers are advised to update to specific versions or later to mitigate the risk.

ClamAV released updates to fix 10 high-severity vulnerabilities that could allow attackers to crash antivirus scanners, trap scan workers in endless loops, or drain system resources. The patches address memory errors and affect various file handling components. Administrators should update to ClamAV 1.5.5 or 1.4.7 for protection.
title: ClamAV Patches 10 High-Severity Vulnerabilities That Could Let Attackers Crash Antivirus Scanners

content: The UK’s Investigatory Powers Tribunal ordered the Home Office to reveal a secret order seeking access to encrypted iCloud data, impacting Apple users. Technical impact includes potential breach of user privacy and data security. Further legal and technical implications to be determined.
title: UK tribunal confirms secret Apple order in iCloud encryption dispute

content: Signal is restricting screenshots on iOS 27 and some Android devices to prevent built-in AI assistants from accessing private chats. The change targets Siri and assistants like Google Gemini, protecting messages from being seen by AI through screen captures. Users can turn off the protection but may expose other messages. Signal is advocating for clearer developer options to control AI access without disabling features.
title: Signal Restricts Screenshots to Protect User Privacy from AI Assistants

content: Hackers exploited misconfigured Temenos Quantum Fabric to gain admin access without passwords, deploying malicious Java components. Affected banks across multiple regions. Malware, named FabricShell and FabricShadow, provided command execution and data exfiltration capabilities. Forescout advises restricting internet access and checking for implants.
title: Hackers Exploit Misconfigured Temenos Banking Platform to Deploy Web Shells Without Passwords
Hackers Breach TfL Oyster Photocard Accounts, Exposing Personal Data of 265,000 Customers
content: Transport for London (TfL) detected a data breach on its Oyster photocard website, exposing personal information such as email addresses, phone numbers, and dates of birth of 265,000 customers. Passwords and payment card details were not compromised. TfL advised affected customers to change matching passwords or security answers on other accounts. The breach highlights the risk of exposed security questions and answers being reused.

title: Chase Announces Vendor Cyberattack May Have Exposed Customer Data
content: JPMorgan Chase reports attackers targeted third-party vendors, potentially exposing customers’ names and email addresses. Visa and Mastercard also disclosed incidents after data theft by a non-extortion group. Mitigation involves assessing vendor security and enhancing data protection measures.

Hackers are scanning LiteLLM AI servers for two critical flaws, CVE-2026-42271 and CVE-2026-48710, which together enable remote code execution. The attacks target unpatched versions of LiteLLM, often found between apps and AI model providers, potentially exposing API keys and other secrets. Teams are advised to upgrade to the latest versions and secure their servers. The technical impact is high, with successful exploitation leading to significant access and potential financial loss.
title: Hackers Actively Scan LiteLLM AI Servers for Critical Flaws Enabling RCE Attacks

content: A cryptographer warns that AI advancements may undermine public-key cryptography systems, posing a 15% risk of losing confidence in existing encryption algorithms. Industry experts debate the need for improved cryptographic agility and caution against hasty changes. Mathematical problems traditionally solved by humans are now being outperformed by AI, raising concerns about cryptographic vulnerabilities.
title: AI Advances Spark Debate on Public-Key Cryptography Security

content: Threat actors use ROMULUS ClickFix to deliver a new RAT, similar to CNCMachineRMS, for spying and controlling PCs. Malware delivery via separate chains, signed binary sideloading techniques. Affects victims targeted by these actors.
title: ROMULUS ClickFix Attacks Deploy RAT to Spy and Control PCs
Wireshark 4.6.10 Released to Patch 39 Security Vulnerabilities
content: Wireshark 4.6.10 addresses 39 security vulnerabilities, including crashes, processing loops, memory leaks, and heap disclosure issues affecting protocol dissectors and capture file parsers. The update is crucial for network troubleshooting and security analysis, with CVEs like CVE-2026-130455 and CVE-2026-130449 addressing critical flaws. Teams should prioritize updating to mitigate risks.

title: Hackers Deploy AI-Assisted PowerShell Toolkit on African Stock Exchange
content: Hackers used an AI-assisted PowerShell toolkit with 41 modules to search for credentials and test access to APIs on a major African stock exchange. The activity, conducted on September 20, 2026, aimed to gain unauthorized access to financial and cloud systems. Security researchers identified six implants linked to Witchetty, a China-linked espionage group. Investigators recommend monitoring DNS queries, API accesses, and endpoint logs for indicators of compromise.

China-nexus group Armory Castle exploited a critical zero-day in VMware vCenter Server (CVE-2026-123890) for admin access and data theft. Technical impact: authentication bypass in VMware Directory Service. Mitigation: Apply patches promptly.
title: China-Linked Hackers Exploit Critical VMware vCenter Zero-Day to Gain Admin Access and Steal Data

content: Hackers published customer data from Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan after cyberattacks on third-party service providers. No breaches occurred at the financial companies themselves. Data exposure included names, email addresses, and marketing details. Companies are investigating vendor breaches and offering support to affected customers.
title: Hackers Leak Customer Data Linked to Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan After Third-Party Cyberattacks
Drupal Fixes Critical RCE Flaw Exploitable by Unauthenticated Hackers
content: Drupal fixed a critical RCE flaw in the installer that could allow unauthenticated attackers to take over vulnerable sites. The bug, CVE-2026-132165, affects Drupal core versions 11.3.x, 11.4.x, and 10.6.x. Administrators should update to 11.3.22, 11.4.13, or 10.6.22 to mitigate risks. The update also addresses a separate moderately critical issue.

A newly disclosed unpatched zero-day technique called FastUnlock allows physical access attackers to run programs on a locked Windows machine without signing in. The attacker gains only a limited account. The vulnerability was posted by researchers MSNightmare and Nightmare Eclipse, and flagged by ThreatLocker.
title: New Unpatched Windows Zero-Day Vulnerability FastUnlock Disclosed

content: A zero-day flaw in Microsoft’s Windows Package Manager (WinGet) allowed a single pull request to potentially compromise moderator GitHub access tokens. This could enable attackers to deploy malicious software updates, access corporate repositories, and steal secrets. Microsoft has patched the issue but advises limiting token scope and validating hosts before attaching credentials. Enterprises must scrutinize internal tools and scripts to mitigate risks.
title: Critical zero-click vulnerability in Microsoft’s WinGet exposes GitHub tokens

content: KPMG Canada confirmed an unauthorized third party accessed confidential tax documents of some clients. Immediate action was taken to secure systems, but details of the breach, including extent and nature of data accessed, remain unclear. Clients should inquire about specific risks to their files.
title: KPMG Canada Confirms Cyberattack on Client Tax Documents
8.8 Million NGINX Services Potentially Exposed to Critical NGINX2Root Vulnerability
content: Around 8.8 million NGINX services are potentially exposed to five memory bugs, allowing unauthenticated users to run commands as a worker process. The most severe bug, CVE-2026-123007, affects versions from 1.9.5 to 1.31.8. Servers must be patched or HTTP/2 disabled to mitigate risk. Censys tracks over 331 million NGINX properties, with 8,823,450 still running affected versions. No exploitation in the wild as of 18 November.

The European Commission was targeted by cyber attackers using the ARTEX tool, shutting down HR systems for over 10 days. No data breach was confirmed, but access controls were compromised. Mitigation included temporarily disabling applications. HR systems are valuable targets for espionage and social engineering.
title: European Commission HR Systems Hit by Cyber Attack
Hackers Exploit VMware vCenter 0-Day Since September to Hijack Admin Accounts and Steal VM Data
content: A suspected China-linked espionage group exploited a VMware vCenter Server zero-day in September 2026, gaining admin access and stealing VM data. The flaw affects VMware Directory Service, allowing networked attackers to bypass authentication. Mitigation involves patching, restricting access, and reviewing logs for signs of compromise.

title: VMware and KVM Vulnerabilities Exploited in Cloud and Virtual Infrastructure
content: VMware issued critical advisories for two vulnerabilities, one allowing unauthorized access to vCenter and the other enabling command execution in SDDC Manager. Apache in Cloud Foundation products also has a remote code execution flaw. KVM disclosed a guest-to-host memory corruption vulnerability affecting AMD processors using nested virtualization. Mitigation involves disabling nested virtualization or applying vendor updates.

title: New Windows 11 Narrator Lock Screen 0-Day Allows Attackers to Bypass BitLocker Protections
content: A newly disclosed Windows 11 zero-day called FastUnlock lets attackers bypass BitLocker protections with physical access. It targets the Narrator screen reader, allowing code execution before sign-in. Mitigation involves limiting physical access to devices.

title: Germ Network Launches Android Messaging Client with End-to-End Encryption
content: Germ Network launched its encrypted messaging client, Germ DM, on Android, seeing a 20x jump in usage. The app uses end-to-end encryption built on Messaging Layer Security and a unique card-based identity system. Bluesky promotes the app for E2E DMs, aiding marketing efforts. Germ aims to offer smart tools for managing social and work life while prioritizing privacy and security.

The AWS Security, Identity, and Governance team hosts re:Invent 2026, focusing on security in the agentic enterprise era. It features over 120 sessions, keynotes, and workshops addressing identity, detection, network protection, and governance. Attendees can participate in hands-on sessions and meet with AWS experts to discuss security challenges.
title: AWS re:Invent 2026 Security Conference
Security Research on Advanced Mitigation Techniques and Vulnerabilities
content: Technical segments on setting up Waydroid and Mitmproxy, along with news on AI in pentesting, RCE vulnerabilities, and AI challenges for defenders. Vulnerability disclosures and exploits continue to rise, with cloud hosts and VMs under threat.

title: Multiple Vulnerabilities in Google Chrome Could Allow for Arbitrary Code Execution
content: Multiple vulnerabilities in Google Chrome could allow for arbitrary code execution. Successful exploitation could lead to installation of programs, data modification, or creation of new accounts with full user rights. Users with administrative privileges are more at risk.

title: OpenSSF Global Cyber Policy Working Group Workshop at Open Source Summit Europe
content: The OpenSSF Global Cyber Policy Working Group held a workshop at Open Source Summit Europe to discuss cybersecurity policy, focusing on the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA). Key areas of discussion included due diligence, vulnerability reporting, and collaboration between manufacturers and maintainers. Participants highlighted the need for practical guidance and tools to address the challenges posed by the CRA.

Third-party breaches at JPMorgan Chase, Visa, and Mastercard may have exposed customer names and email addresses. No payment data was affected. Financial firms are investigating but declined to disclose further details on the breach or the affected third-party providers.
title: JPMorgan Chase, Visa, and Mastercard confirm third-party cyberattacks potentially exposing customer data

content: AWS has introduced a new security analytics dashboard for AWS WAF to help investigate traffic and contain threats more efficiently. The dashboard provides a unified view across multiple protection packs and dimensions, enabling faster threat response and reducing false positives. It allows filtering, grouping, and detailed inspection of traffic data.
title: Introducing the New AWS WAF Security Analytics Dashboard

content: A severe authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-123890) in VMware vCenter was patched, enabling unauthorized access. Patches are available for VMware vCenter 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200, and 8.0 U3m. Other issues include SQL injection, command injection, privilege escalation, and SAML token bypass vulnerabilities, rated from Important to Moderate. Immediate patching is advised.
title: Critical flaw in VMware vCenter allows authentication bypass
Third-Party JavaScript Compromise Compromises Multiple Websites
content: A recent supply-chain attack exploited a weakness in a vendor’s platform, modifying third-party JavaScript to steal payment card details, tamper with cryptocurrency transactions, and send cookies to attacker-controlled servers. Multiple websites of well-known brands were affected. Mitigation involves a strict Content Security Policy, inventorying third-party scripts, and monitoring changes.

Visitors to websites of well-known brands were served malicious JavaScript via a third-party web service, stealing payment card details and tampering with cryptocurrency transactions. Organizations did not deploy bad code themselves but relied on a vendor’s platform. Content Security Policy (CSP) with strict script-src settings could prevent attacks. Organizations should inventory third-party scripts, enforce CSP, and monitor for changes.
title: Third-Party JavaScript Compromise Affects Multiple Organizations

content: A Russian national, Igor D’iu, was indicted for surveilling employees of a Silicon Valley company assisting Ukraine. He photographed employees and their screens, tracked home addresses, and followed a worker, causing emotional distress. The incident highlights cyber espionage risks in tech and defense sectors.
title: Russian Spy Indicted for Surveillance of Silicon Valley Tech and Defense Company

content: Drupal core versions prior to 10.6.22, 11.3.22, and 11.4.13 are affected by vulnerabilities, including a critical remote code execution flaw. Users and administrators are advised to review the provided web link and apply necessary updates.
title: Drupal Security Advisory (AV26-1186)

content: AWS Security Incident Response processes and triages threat findings from Amazon GuardDuty and AWS Security Hub, categorizing findings into archival, case opening, or review. Most findings are handled automatically, reducing noise for security teams. Key findings like credential exfiltration are escalated for further investigation.
title: AWS Security Incident Response Workflow and Triage Process
VMware Security Advisory (AV26-1185) – Update 1
content: VMware products are affected by vulnerabilities, with CVE-2026-123890 exploited in the wild. CISA added the vulnerability to their KEV database. Users are advised to review and apply necessary updates.

title: Mitel Security Advisory (AV26-1184)
content: Mitel products, specifically MiCollab versions prior to or equal to 10.3 (10.3.0.18), are affected by vulnerabilities. Users and administrators are advised to review the provided web links and apply necessary updates to mitigate potential exploits.

title: Nvidia under investigation for possible data breach by ransomware group
content: Nvidia is investigating a possible data breach claimed by ransomware group The Gentlemen's affiliates. While Nvidia denies system involvement, the group has a history of prolific attacks. The breach could affect sensitive company information, and Nvidia faces ongoing cybersecurity challenges.

title: Ubiquiti Security Advisory (AV26-1182)
content: Ubiquiti is affected by vulnerabilities in UniFi Access Application prior to 4.3.24. Users and administrators are advised to review the security advisory and apply necessary updates.
PHP Group advises users to update to versions 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, 8.5.13, and 8.6.0 to address vulnerabilities. Users and administrators should review the provided links for updates.
title: PHP Group Security Advisory (AV26-1183)
JetBrains Security Advisory (AV26-1181)
content: JetBrains products, particularly TeamCity versions prior to 2026.2.1 and 2026.1.5, are affected by vulnerabilities. Users and administrators are advised to review and apply necessary updates to mitigate risks.

title: CraftCMS Security Advisory (AV26-1180)
content: CraftCMS versions prior to 5.11.5 are affected by vulnerabilities. The Cyber Centre advises users to review security advisories and apply necessary updates.

The FBI pretended to be both a ransomware victim and threat actor to target a Florida-based company run by Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar. The firm claimed to offer data recovery services for ransomware victims, but was actually a scam. Technical impact and mitigation details not provided.
title: FBI Posed as Victim and Attacker to Catch Ransomware Scammer

content: A fake Elon Musk livestream tricked Coinbase users into sending $4.7 million in crypto to scammers. Scammers used a deepfake to impersonate Musk, prompting users to send cryptocurrency. Automated defenses stopped about 91% of the attempted transfers. To avoid such scams, users should be wary of unsolicited payment requests, especially those linked to celebrity impersonations.
title: Deepfake Elon Musk scam nearly costs viewers $4.7 million in crypto

content: A vulnerability in PHP's file-based session storage allows object injection, enabling code execution. Affected are users of PHP applications. Mitigation: Update to fixed PHP releases. Technical Impact: Severe, as it bypasses security measures. Response: Apply updates immediately.
title: PHP's phpAfterShell Flaw Exposed: Object Injection Leads to Code Execution

content: A deepfake of Elon Musk was used in a crypto scam, tricking Coinbase users into sending $4.7 million in attempts. The scam relied on convincing victims to send cryptocurrency to a fake address, bypassing automated defenses. Users were logged in and confirmed the transactions themselves. To stay safe, avoid sending funds to unverified sources and check offers critically.
title: Fake Elon Musk livestream scam nearly costs viewers $4.7 million in crypto
Multiple Vulnerabilities in NGINX Could Allow for Remote Code Execution
content: Multiple vulnerabilities in NGINX could allow for remote code execution. NGINX is used for web serving, reverse proxying, caching, and load balancing. Exploitation could lead to remote code execution with potential impact depending on user rights.

title: New phpAfterShell Attack Bypasses PHP2Shell Fix to Enable Remote Code Execution
content: A new PHP vulnerability, phpAfterShell, allows unauthenticated remote code execution despite October patches for PHP2Shell. The flaw affects PHP’s session handler during upload progress. Applications using file-based sessions are at risk. Mitigation includes upgrading PHP and disabling session upload progress.

title: Critical VMware vCenter Flaws Let Hackers Bypass Authentication and Access Servers
content: VMware vCenter and SDDC Manager flaws let attackers bypass authentication, gaining full control. CVSS scores range from 6.7 to 9.8. Patches are available, but no workarounds exist. Admins must apply updates and restrict network access to vCenter systems.

A Russian national, Igor D'iu, was arrested for allegedly spying on a US defense tech company in Palo Alto, conducting surveillance and collecting data via remote access devices. FBI agents found evidence linking his activities to the Russian Federal Security Service (FSB). He is charged with spying offenses and fake identity document creation.
title: Russian National Indicted for Espionage Against US Defense Tech Company in Palo Alto
JPMorgan Chase Confirms Third-Party Cyberattack That May Have Exposed Customer Names and Emails
content: A cyberattack targeted third-party service providers to JPMorgan Chase, potentially exposing customer names and email addresses. The breach did not disrupt banking services but may enable phishing attacks. Customers will receive notifications and free credit monitoring. The attack’s technical details remain unclear.

AI assistants in company computers can be exploited by attackers. Risks include unauthorized use, excessive permissions, and direct malware deployment via language models. Security measures like application control, web filtering, and threat intelligence are recommended. Response includes monitoring, allowlisting, and limiting outbound connections.
title: Protecting Against AI-Driven Attacks | Kaspersky
High-End Furniture Marketplace AptDeco Faces Seller Payment Delays and Customer Complaints
content: AptDeco, a high-end furniture marketplace, has faced issues with delayed payments to sellers and customer complaints. Sellers report not receiving payments for months despite products being collected. The company attributes the issue to bot swarms and is currently resolving the problem. Customers are considering legal action.
F5 BIG-IP and related products are affected by multiple vulnerabilities. Users are advised to update to the latest versions to mitigate risks.
title: F5 Security Advisory (AV26-1178)
Proton Drive Adds Direct Imports from Google Drive
content: Proton Drive introduces Easy Switch for direct file imports from Google Drive, enhancing user migration. Available in Proton Drive’s web app across all plans, this feature simplifies data transfer, initially rolled out gradually.
OpenVPN prior to 2.7.8 is affected by a vulnerability. The Cyber Centre advises users and administrators to review web links and apply necessary updates to mitigate the risk.
title: OpenVPN Security Advisory (AV26-1179)
Google extends retention of Gemini chat data
content: Google is extending the retention period of Gemini chat data to about two months, even when chat history is turned off. This change affects both temporary and newly started conversations. The update impacts user data privacy and regulatory compliance.

Criminal IP launched AITEM, integrating asset discovery, public-source exposure analysis, and dark web monitoring with AI. It helps teams understand and manage exposure across their infrastructure and web assets, offering continuous monitoring and AI-assisted validation of security risks.
title: Criminal IP Launches AITEM for AI-Powered Asset Discovery and Exposure Management

content: A zero-day flaw in VMware vCenter allows network attackers to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access. Affects the central console for managing ESX hosts and VMs. Fixed versions available, but no workaround provided.
title: Critical VMware vCenter Zero-Day Flaw Enables Bypass of Authentication

content: A critical vulnerability in Drupal core allows unauthenticated attackers to reinstall sites, potentially leading to site takeover or remote code execution. Fixed releases for all supported branches were issued. Common but uncommonly configured sites are at risk.
title: Drupal Patches Critical Installer Flaw for Unauthenticated Attackers

content: Ransomware attacks involve credential theft, lateral movement, and security control disablement before data encryption. Acronis highlights five indicators to detect intrusions early, contain malicious activity, and protect systems and backups.
title: Five warning signs of ransomware breach before encryption or data theft

content: The PHP Foundation released security updates to fix 7 critical flaws, including remote code execution bugs. Affected deployments could be exploited. Users of all supported PHP versions should update immediately to mitigate risks.
title: PHP Addresses 7 Critical Flaws, Including Remote Code Execution Bugs
Study Reveals Racial Disparities in Data Center Location
content: A study found that Black neighborhoods are twice as likely to house data centers compared to white neighborhoods. Researchers analyzed 81,000 US census tracts and 5,291 data centers, attributing the disparity to historical redlining and infrastructure placement. The study suggests data center-specific zoning and racial impact statements to address the issue.
A security breach compromised account details of 265,000 Oyster photocard customers. TfL has taken its portal offline and contained the incident. The breach was discovered on November 16, 2026.
title: TfL breach exposed data of 265,000 Oyster photocard customers

content: PHP released critical security updates for all supported versions, addressing remote code execution and other severe vulnerabilities. Website operators and hosting providers are advised to update promptly. Vulnerabilities require uncommon setups, so risks vary. Administrators should follow the project’s changelog and patch all affected branches.
title: PHP Urges Users to Update Due to Critical Security Flaws

content: ICE is paying AT&T millions to access trillions of phone records and location data. The program likely affects AT&T customers and non-customers. Experts raise concerns over potential misuse and lack of judicial oversight.
title: ICE Pays AT&T for Access to Massive Phone Records
Meta’s AI Agent Muse Exploits Android and Mac Permissions to Read Encrypted Messages
content: Meta’s AI agent Muse read Signal messages on Android and Macs through notification and screen access, despite not directly connecting to the app. This demonstrates the technical risk of granting broad permissions to AI assistants, potentially exposing sensitive information. Users should review and limit permissions for such apps.

BADBOX 3.0 malware infected low-cost Android streaming boxes, generating 40 billion fraudulent ad requests daily. The malware played ads outside the visible screen and borrowed names of legitimate apps. It also enrolled devices in residential proxy networks. Satori Threat Intelligence identified and disrupted the campaign, recommending buyers verify Play Protect certification before purchase.
title: BADBOX 3.0 Malware Infects Android TV Boxes to Generate 40 Billion Fraudulent Ad Requests Daily

content: A Russian-speaking cybercrime operation steals login credentials for US banks, IRS, and Social Security from infected Windows PCs. Despite victims using password managers and MFA, the malware broke Chrome and Edge encryption to steal passwords. Indicators of compromise include specific server IPs and domains. Victims should use clean devices to change passwords and block listed IPs and domains.
title: Malware Steals US Bank, IRS, and Social Security Login Credentials from Infected Windows PCs
Cultural Impact of Grand Theft Auto Across Two Decades of News Coverage
content: This article chronicles how Grand Theft Auto has been covered by news media since 2001, reflecting cultural and societal changes over two decades. Initially, the games were vilified for violence and sexual content, leading to congressional hearings and moral panics. Over time, the focus shifted to the game's financial success and its role in the entertainment industry. The coverage now emphasizes economic concerns rather than moral objections. The impact on the gaming industry, including job losses, is also discussed.

CISA added four flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog after finding evidence of active exploitation. Affected products include Synology, BerriAI LiteLLM, Apache Axis, and REDCap. Exploits range from code execution to unauthorized access. Administrators should apply the latest patches and check for signs of compromise before and after updates.
title: CISA Warns Hackers Are Actively Exploiting Four Flaws in Synology, LiteLLM, Apache Axis and REDCap
Chrome Updates Patch Six Critical Flaws, Including AI-Found Bugs
content: Google patched six critical vulnerabilities in Chrome 158, all memory-safety errors, with two found by AI. The update affects Windows, Mac, Linux, and Android. Users should update to mitigate risks.

title: Google patches six critical Chrome flaws, two found with AI
content: Google released Chrome 158 with 204 security fixes, including six critical vulnerabilities found with AI. The critical flaws affect GPU, Media, WebView, and more, posing a significant risk of memory corruption. Users are advised to update Chrome to mitigate risks.

A Russian national was indicted for spying on a Silicon Valley defense company using remote access tools and following employees. The operation aimed to gather information about employees and their home addresses. The incident highlights the risks for defense firms and the importance of monitoring for unauthorized surveillance.
title: Russian National Accused of Using Remote Access Tools to Spy on Silicon Valley Defense Firm
Attackers Exploit PHP Vulnerabilities in PAN-OS Management Interfaces
content: Attackers exploited two PHP vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) against PAN-OS management interfaces. This allowed unauthenticated code execution on web servers. Palo Alto Networks confirmed the issue on October 28, 2023. Mitigation involves patching and securing exposed management interfaces.

title: Hackers Exploit Microsoft 365 Device Code Authentication to Hijack Accounts and Bypass MFA
content: Hackers trick employees with fake payment notices and SharePoint documents, leading them to a genuine Microsoft sign-in page and hijacking accounts. The technique does not break MFA or steal passwords. Security teams should filter authentication logs for device code flows and block them where possible. Indicators of compromise include specific domains and SHA-256 hashes.

A data breach at software provider Wellington IT exposed saved payee details from 40 Irish credit unions. Affected credit unions reported that names, BICs, IBANs, and addresses were compromised. Wellington IT notified credit unions after the vulnerability was exploited between October 2-4, closing the flaw on October 6. The breach is criticized for delayed notification and prompts an investigation by Irish authorities.
title: Cyberattack on service provider exposes payee data at 40 Irish credit unions
Palo Alto Networks Acquires Applied Compute for $4.5B to Enhance AI Security Solutions
content: Palo Alto Networks acquired Applied Compute for $4.5 billion to integrate AI models into its security products. The deal will enable secure, open-weight AI implementations for enterprises. Mitigation involves securing trained models and ensuring compliance with jurisdictional regulations.

A North Korea-linked hacking group, Kimsuky, used aNotepad to deliver XenoRAT and NodeLinkRAT backdoors to South Korean policy and security professionals via spearphishing. The attackers switched malware without changing the initial payload, making detection challenging. They stole documents and financial details. Defenses should monitor for LNK file executions, scheduled tasks, and memory scripts.
title: Hackers Use aNotepad as a Malware Delivery Channel for XenoRAT and NodeLinkRAT Backdoors
How to tell a cyberattack from a plain old outage
content: Over the past week, multiple IT outages affected various companies and government agencies in the US, raising concerns of a cyberattack, but no evidence supports foul play. Cybersecurity analysts are needed to distinguish between technical failures and cyberattacks.

Transport for London (TfL) reported a data breach affecting around 265,000 Oyster photocard customers, with emails sent from TfL's systems misleading users. No passwords, bank details, or journey information were compromised, but customers are advised to change passwords and security questions. TfL has taken down the website for investigation and notified the ICO.
title: TfL Compromises Oyster Photocard Customer Accounts

content: N-able confirmed unauthorized access to a server in its Mail Assure and SpamExperts hosted cloud environment, disabling management access across three regions. Email filtering continued, but API and dashboard access were restricted. No evidence of customer data compromise found. Ongoing investigation.
title: N-able Confirms Server Breach, Disables Management Access
Sticky note exposure leads to full network access and data theft
content: A password on a sticky note led to full network access, exposing HR, salary, and accounting data. The pen tester gained access through the sticky note, showing the importance of physical security and proper access controls. The company disabled the account, reviewed logs, and tightened file share permissions.

title: Ubiquiti Warns of Critical UniFi Access Flaws Enabling Root Code Execution Attacks
content: Ubiquiti disclosed seven vulnerabilities in its UniFi Access Application, allowing attackers with limited network permissions to execute code as root. Five critical flaws could lead to full host control, while others expose sensitive information or allow SSRF. Administrators should update to version 4.3.24 or later and restrict network access.

CISA warned of four exploited vulnerabilities affecting Synology DSM, BerriAI LiteLLM, Apache Axis, and Vanderbilt REDCap, linked to ransomware and cryptomining. Organizations are urged to update and patch systems promptly to mitigate risks.
title: CISA Warns of Exploited Vulnerabilities Linked to Ransomware and Cryptomining
Hackers Target European Commission with ARTEX AI Tool in Major Cyberattack
content: A cyberattack on the European Commission disrupted staff services for over 10 days. Hackers used an AI tool called ARTEX to target systems handling payslips, leave requests, and medical reimbursements. The extent of data access remains unclear, and the Commission is investigating. Mitigation efforts include conducting extra security checks and briefings for commissioners.

title: Hackers Breach N-able Cloud Server, Disrupting Email Security Management Across 3 Regions
content: Threat actors breached N-able’s Mail Assure and Spam Experts Hosted Cloud, disabling management interfaces and APIs. Impacted regions: 3. Mitigation efforts are underway to harden services.

title: Scattered Spider's Phishing and SIM-Swap Tactics Led to Six-Year Sentence
content: Scattered Spider used phishing texts and SIM swaps to steal $11.6 million in cryptocurrency. Tyler Robert Buchanan, a 24-year-old British man, was sentenced to six years in prison. Phishing texts and SIM swaps compromised company systems and personal accounts. Experts predict the group is fragmented but still active.

Scattered Spider used phishing texts and SIM swaps to steal $11.6 million in cryptocurrency. Tyler Robert Buchanan was sentenced to six years in prison. The group targeted at least a dozen companies and used stolen credentials to access systems. SIM swapping allowed them to take over cryptocurrency accounts. The group is fragmented, with multiple members arrested in different countries.
title: Scattered Spider’s Phishing and SIM-Swap Tactics Result in Six-Year Sentence
Vulnerability Management: The True Challenge Lies in Effective Remediation
content: The cybersecurity industry has long focused on identifying and prioritizing vulnerabilities, but the real challenge is getting remediation done. Large organizations struggle with organizational bottlenecks, governance, and resource allocation. AI is increasing vulnerability discovery, but may exacerbate remediation backlogs. Effective remediation requires a robust operating model to ensure accountability and coordination across teams.

title: Critical One-Byte Heap Overflow in Ruby Could Allow RCE Attacks
content: A critical memory corruption flaw in Ruby’s string case conversion code allows remote code execution (RCE). Affects Ruby 3.3.0-3.3.13, 3.4.0-3.4.12, and 4.0.0-4.0.9. Exploitation can be reached through upcase, swapcase, downcase(: fold), and casecmp?. Veria Labs identified affected Ruby runtimes in popular self-hosted software like GitLab, GitHub Enterprise Server, and Mastodon. Updating to fixed releases is crucial to mitigate the risk.

title: Splunk Patches Critical 9.9 RCE and Authentication Bypass Vulnerabilities in SOAR and Enterprise
content: Splunk released updates to fix critical remote code execution and authentication bypass vulnerabilities in Splunk SOAR and Enterprise. The flaws, including CVE-2026-131253 and CVE-2026-76535, require separate patches for different products. Impact includes unauthorized code execution and data access. Administrators should upgrade to the latest versions and verify patch installation.

Seven memory-safety flaws in Ruby's regular expression engine and string case-conversion code were fixed. PoCs for five flaws show remote code execution is possible. Default Rails apps are at risk. Users should update to latest versions immediately.
title: Ruby Releases Patches for Seven Memory-Safety Flaws, Some Potentially Exploitable
Hackers Deploy Overlord RAT That Survives Windows Resets and Crashes Systems When Terminated
content: A financially motivated group is deploying Overlord RAT, a Windows remote access trojan that persists after system resets and triggers a blue screen if forcefully terminated. The campaign targets cryptocurrency holders, gaming account owners, and users of internet calling software. The malware uses two persistence methods: registry entries and tampering with the Windows Recovery Environment. It also includes 35 commands for data exfiltration. Indicators of compromise include specific IP addresses and command servers.

title: Ruby Patches 7 Security Vulnerabilities, Including Buffer Overflow and RCE Flaws
content: Ruby 4.0.10, 3.4.13, and 3.3.14 patched seven security vulnerabilities, including RCE and buffer overflow, affecting Ruby’s regular expression engine and string case-conversion code. Users are urged to upgrade to mitigate potential attacks. Impacted versions are Ruby 3.3.13 and earlier, 3.4.0 through 3.4.12, and 4.0.0 through 4.0.9.

Researcher shows low-privilege database accounts can be used to run code on the server via memory-corruption bugs in SQL engine code. Impacts PostgreSQL, MySQL, ClickHouse, and Oracle. Mitigation: Apply vendor patches, limit database privileges.
title: Researcher Demonstrates Database RCE Exploits Affecting PostgreSQL, MySQL and Oracle
Signal Introduces AI Screenshots Block to Protect Chat Privacy
content: Signal restricts AI agents from reading private chats via screenshots on Android and iOS to enhance privacy. However, the protection is incomplete. This affects users of agentic systems in iOS 27 and Android versions with encrypted messaging capabilities.

Hackers exploit critical vulnerabilities in Apache, Cisco, and VMware systems for espionage. The U.S. CISA added four flaws to its KEV list, with CVE-2026-129448 rated CVSS 9.8. Affected are Apache Roller, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver, and VMware vCenter. Organizations must patch and monitor for exploits.
title: Hackers Exploit Critical VMware, Cisco, and Apache Flaws as Espionage Attacks Emerge

content: F5 released emergency fixes for six critical BIG-IP vulnerabilities that could allow remote attackers to crash services or execute code. These data-plane flaws impact specific configurations, affecting traffic management and potentially leading to website outages. Affected versions include BIG-IP, BIG-IP Next for Kubernetes, and BIG-IP Cloud-Native Network Functions. Immediate patching and testing are advised to mitigate risks.
title: 6 Critical F5 BIG-IP Vulnerabilities Could Let Hackers Disrupt Websites and Execute Malicious Code
WhatsApp Android Flaws Could Let Hackers Delete Users’ Files and Expose IP Addresses
content: WhatsApp's November 2026 update addresses three flaws: file deletion, IP exposure, and a certificate check bypass. Attackers could exploit these to delete local files or expose users' IP addresses. Users should update to the latest version to mitigate risks.

title: PHP2Shell Aftershock: 18 Security Flaws Patched
content: PHP released patches for 18 vulnerabilities, including a critical request smuggling flaw that could enable remote code execution (RCE). Enterprises should patch all supported versions to mitigate risks, especially as PHP2Shell vulnerabilities have already caused widespread concern. Security teams must inventory and patch all PHP deployments quickly.

The CTO of ransomwarehelp.com, a company that purported to help victims recover encrypted data, was indicted for wire fraud. He paid ransomware groups for decryption keys and marked up the fees for victims. The company claimed to offer advanced cryptographic tools but was found to be fraudulent. This case highlights the fraudulent nature of some ransomware help services and underscores the importance of choosing reputable firms.
title: CTO of RansomwareHelp Indicted for Wire Fraud
F5 Releases Critical Patches for BIG-IP Vulnerabilities
content: F5 released out-of-band patches for BIG-IP Access Policy Manager and iRule, five of which are rated critical. These patches address stack-based buffer overflows that could lead to remote code execution. BIG-IP is used for application access management and traffic handling. F5 advises immediate hotfix installation and upgrade to patched versions to mitigate risks.

PHP 8.6 addresses seven critical remote code execution (RCE) flaws, tightening session security by enabling Strict Mode, HttpOnly, and SameSite settings by default. This mitigates session hijacking and cross-site request forgery. Additionally, stricter handling of null values and other security functions are introduced to prevent data integrity issues. While these changes enhance security, administrators must ensure configurations are updated to gain full benefits.
title: PHP 8.6: Addressing Remote Code Execution Flaws and Enhancing Security Defaults
Vulnerability in VMware vCenter Could Allow Authentication Bypass
content: A vulnerability in VMware vCenter could allow unauthenticated attackers to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access, potentially leading to data manipulation or account creation with full user rights.

Visa and Mastercard suffered data breaches by ransomware and extortion group n0n, which leaked customer data including mobile numbers, BIN prefixes, and booking details. No financial details like card numbers or passwords were compromised, potentially leaving customers vulnerable to phishing attacks. Financial firms are investigating the breach, attributing it to a third-party provider, with Qubole being a suspected access path.
title: Visa, Mastercard Data Breach Lacks Financial Details but Contains Sensitive Information
Multiple Vulnerabilities in Mitel MiCollab Could Allow for Arbitrary Code Execution
content: Multiple vulnerabilities in Mitel MiCollab could allow arbitrary code execution. Mitel MiCollab is a unified communications platform. Successful exploitation could result in data manipulation or full system compromise. Mitigation involves timely patching and least privilege access.

A researcher planted 2 million digital tripwires in AI services to test for data leaks, uncovering widespread privacy violations and security breaches. Sensitive information, including AWS access keys and SSH passwords, was exposed through various AI router services. The experiment highlighted the risks in AI app development and usage, emphasizing the need for better security measures.
title: Researcher plants 2m canaries in AI supply chain to expose data leaks
Signal restricts AI agents to protect user privacy
content: Signal, an encrypted messaging app, restricts access to user messages by AI agents like Google Gemini and Apple Siri unless explicit permission is granted. This move aims to protect privacy by preventing these AI systems from accessing sensitive communications. Apple and Google are integrating AI capabilities into their operating systems, potentially compromising user data. Signal's implementation of screenshot blocking on iOS and Android apps is a partial solution, but it highlights the broader issue of AI agents undermining application privacy.
The podcast covers AI fraud, an AI agent suing Meta, and the use of AI detection tools by the Department of Justice. No clear technical incident or exploit is described.
title: Podcast Discusses AI-Driven Cyber Threats

content: Multiple critical vulnerabilities in nginx versions 1.9.5 through 1.31.8, affecting Cisco products, were announced. These vulnerabilities could lead to remote code execution and are fixed in nginx releases 1.31.9 (mainline) and 1.30.7 (stable). CVEs include CVE-2026-113425, CVE-2026-121810, CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633, and CVE-2026-123634. Security Impact Rating: Critical.
title: Vulnerabilities in nginx Affecting Cisco Products: November 2026
Cisco Security Advisory - Update 1 for Known Exploited Vulnerabilities
content: Cisco is affected by multiple vulnerabilities across various products. As of November 20, 2026, CVE-2026-76466 was added to CISA's KEV database, indicating active exploitation. Users are advised to review and apply necessary updates.

SAP released security advisories for multiple products in November 2025 to address vulnerabilities. CISA added a new CVE to their KEV database on November 20, 2026. Users are advised to review the advisories, apply necessary updates, and implement suggested mitigations.
title: SAP Security Advisory – November 2025 Monthly Rollup (AV25-738) – Update 1

content: WhatsApp addressed 3 security flaws, one impacting Android, suspected in scam messages. CVE-2026-23871, a URL validation issue, was patched. Users should update to version 2.26.17.4.
title: WhatsApp Patches Security Flaws, Suspected Exploit in Android Scams
Mitigating Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) with TruRisk Eliminate
content: Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) is a heap out-of-bounds write in the AVX-512 Base64 decoder of HotSpot JVM on x86-64 CPUs. It allows pre-authentication remote code execution in several Java applications. OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later, and versions 18 to 27, are affected. Oracle released fixed builds on November 17, 2026. Qualys offers a mitigation with TruRisk Eliminate, which automatically targets Linux and Windows hosts with AVX-512 VBMI CPUs and affected Java runtimes, adding -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics to JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS. Untested containers require manual setting of the flag.

Java4Shell is a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the AVX-512 Base64 decoder of the HotSpot JVM on x86-64. Affected versions include Oracle Java 17.0.6 and later, and OpenJDK 18 to 27 below the fixed builds. As of November 17, 2026, no wild exploitation has been reported, but researchers demonstrated pre-authentication remote code execution. Organizations are advised to patch affected Java versions or mitigate by starting the JVM with -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics. Qualys offers TruRisk Eliminate to automatically apply this mitigation on eligible hosts.
title: Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) Exploit Mitigation via TruRisk Eliminate
Chinese-nexus actor’s Cairn AI agents found a zero-day on their own
content: A Chinese-nexus threat actor used autonomous AI agents with Cairn to find a zero-day in an open-source medical imaging application, gaining full control of a server. The agents persisted against hardened targets for 16 hours. Defenders should prepare for rapid AI-driven attacks and prioritize automated responses.

title: UK cybersecurity operation prevents fridge and freezer cyber-attack
content: A UK government operation prevented a cyber-attack on fridges and freezers in supermarkets, warehouses, restaurants, petrol stations, and stadiums. The attack would have been similar to those in Europe causing significant damage. Many retailers remain vulnerable.

Microsoft has been named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for SIEM. The recognition highlights Microsoft Sentinel’s comprehensive SIEM capabilities, including advanced analytics, automation, and threat intelligence, which help organizations protect their digital estates. Microsoft Defender’s Integrated Security Operations Center (ISOC) further integrates SIEM with XDR, AI, and native protection for faster threat response.
title: Microsoft Recognized as a Leader in Gartner Magic Quadrant for SIEM

content: China-linked attackers used AI agents to find and exploit a zero-day in MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging application, gaining full control of a university server. The agents also attempted multiple other attacks before successfully exploiting the zero-day. Amazon notified the maintainers, who released a fix and advisory.
title: Chinese attackers used AI to exploit a zero-day in MONAI Label
Microsoft Recognized as a Leader in Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for SIEM
content: Microsoft was recognized as a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for SIEM, highlighting its comprehensive SIEM capabilities across the digital estate. Microsoft Sentinel integrates security data, advanced analytics, automation, and threat intelligence, supporting threat hunting, investigation, and response. The Integrated Security Operations Center (ISOC) in Microsoft Defender reimagines security operations, combining SIEM with XDR, threat intelligence, and response for faster threat detection and disruption.

title: Microsoft Investigates Attachment Upload Failures in New Outlook
content: Microsoft is investigating issues with attachment uploads in New Outlook. Users can work around the issue by using the Outlook on the web or classic Outlook. A fix is under development but not yet deployed.

A new Android malware framework called Bazuka uses fake screen overlays to steal credentials and control devices. Discovered by ThreatFabric, it integrates LLM for victim management. Affects Android users, poses significant security risks.
title: Bazuka Android Malware Uses Fake Screen Overlays for Credential Theft and Device Control
Over 100 Debian Packages Still Contain Distrusted CA Certificates Despite Security Updates
content: More than 100 Debian packages retained distrusted CA certificates after updates. This shows why trust store updates may not affect all applications. Administrators must ensure their applications use the latest trust store. Technical impact includes potential for certificate-based attacks. Mitigation involves checking and updating local trust stores.

The Dutch Data Protection Authority (AP) warned consumers against AI-powered smart glasses due to safety concerns, including incorrect advice and privacy violations. Testing revealed issues such as dim or coverable recording lights and ability to bypass security. The AP advised banning smart glasses where necessary and called for ethical considerations in AI development.
title: Dutch Data Protection Authority Warns Against AI-Powered Smart Glasses

content: This week's Behind the Blog focuses on the online discourse surrounding a famous hippo incident, highlighting the rapid rise of expertise and toxicity in social media. No specific technical impact or affected parties are mentioned.
title: Behind the Blog: Keeping It Together
Moxa issues security advisory for product vulnerabilities (AV26-1187)
content: Moxa has released a security advisory for vulnerabilities in multiple product series, including ioLogik E1200, EDS-E, IKS, ICS, PT, SDS, TWS, and TN. Affected firmware versions are all prior to v4.0. The Cyber Centre recommends reviewing provided links and applying necessary updates.

title: Still tracking company passwords in spreadsheets? You’re flying blind.
content: Centralized password management improves credential visibility, identifies risks, and simplifies secure sharing. Spreadsheets pose security risks by storing weak, reused, or compromised credentials outside approved systems.

Noteworthy stories that might have slipped under the radar: EU sanctions NoName057(16), malware targets CACs, Gemini agents targeted Epoch AI. Impact on cybersecurity landscape, potential for broader threats.
title: In Other News: Norwegian Energy Firm Cyberattacks, Supercomputer Hack, New Nightmare Eclipse Exploit
Noteworthy Cybersecurity Stories
content: EU sanctions NoName057(16), malware targets CACs, and Gemini agents hit. Multiple unrelated cybersecurity incidents reported.

title: Critical Apache Tomcat Flaw Lets Remote Attackers Join Trusted Server Clusters Without Authentication
content: A critical flaw in Apache Tomcat allows remote attackers to join trusted server clusters without authentication. This affects versions 11.0.28-29 and 10.1.62-9.0.124 when using TLS 1.3 with a pre-shared key. Apache recommends switching to TLS 1.2 and updating to fixed versions pending release. Mitigation involves checking cluster settings and reviewing logs.

title: US launches center to disrupt scams and warn victims sooner
content: The US establishes the Threat Disruption Center to connect investigators with companies for rapid intervention against scams. It aims to freeze funds, take down malicious domains, and ban scammers’ accounts. Beneficiaries include cryptocurrency users, social network users, and victims of cybercrime. Early reporting to the FBI’s IC3 is crucial for effective response.

The US launches the Threat Disruption Center to connect investigators with companies to interrupt scam infrastructure and help victims. The center aims to freeze funds, take down malicious domains, and ban scammers’ accounts. Beneficiaries include anyone targeted by scams, cybercrime, and sextortion. Victims are advised to report scams immediately to the FBI’s IC3.
title: US Launches Threat Disruption Center to Combat Scams

content: Signal updated iOS 27 and Android devices to block screenshots to avoid AI assistants like Siri and Gemini from reading private conversations. This update extends previous protections against Microsoft Recall. The change aims to safeguard user privacy.
title: Signal restricts screenshots to prevent AI assistants from accessing private chats
Hackers Use 355 Domains to Spread Fake GTA 6 PC Launchers Delivering Malware
content: Hackers spread malware through fake GTA 6 PC launchers on 355 domains. Victims downloading the ZIP archive run malicious programs. Security teams should monitor DNS and web proxy logs for IoCs and verify downloads through official channels.

A ransomware group leaked data including emails, phone numbers, and travel or dining bookings from third-party service providers linked to Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan customers. No payment data was exposed. Companies acknowledged incidents but reported no impact to their payment networks. Customers should verify messages and use Malwarebytes Scam Guard to protect their accounts.
title: Hackers leak data linked to Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan customers

content: A ransomware group leaked customer data from third-party service providers linked to Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan. The data includes emails, phone numbers, and travel or dining bookings. Cybercriminals could exploit this information for phishing attacks. JPMorgan, Visa, and Mastercard reported no impact to payment networks, but the leak poses risks to customer security.
title: Hackers leak data linked to Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan customers

content: Hackers modified the SoftEther VPN Bridge, known as NtMonitor, to quietly link external networks to victim’s local networks, aiding espionage. Linked to Webworm, a China-aligned group, this tool was used post-breach to maintain access without detection. Defenders should inventory approved services, monitor unexpected services, and collect IoCs for analysis.
title: Hackers Rebuild Legitimate VPN Software for Espionage
OpenSSL Hit by Critical 9.8 Heap Buffer Overflow Vulnerability in Base64 Encoding Function
content: A critical heap buffer overflow vulnerability in OpenSSL’s Base64 encoding function can corrupt application memory when processing large inputs. This flaw affects versions 4.0.0 through 4.0.3 and 4.1.0, with fixes in 4.0.4 and 4.1.1. Security teams should check for untrusted data usage and enforce input limits before encoding, ensuring all OpenSSL copies across systems, containers, and applications are updated and verified.

title: KVM Hypervisor Vulnerability CVE-2026-99312 Allows Guest VMs to Access Host Memory
content: A vulnerability in KVM, the Linux hypervisor, lets guest VMs access host memory on AMD-hosted servers. This affects DigitalOcean shared servers with nested virtualization.
